final.investment_thesis:
The two sides are not arguing about the same thing, and that asymmetry decides the call. The bear conceded the fundamental case outright — 'excellent' quarter, ~34.2x rather than 41x at the $313.33 close, the 200-SMA at 279.41 rising with price ~12% above it, $62.2B of net cash, and an explicit refusal to call AAPL a short. The undisputed numbers are the strongest in the file: revenue +16.4%, gross margin 50.06% (+357bp, third consecutive quarter of expansion up the 47.0 → 48.6 → 50.1 ladder), EPS +28.7%, FCF +52.5% at a 30.2% margin, a −63 day cash conversion cycle, and net cash UP $28.4B while management returned $73.9B and cut D/E from 1.34x to 0.78x. The bear's own prescription — 'hold at 60–70% of normal sizing, do not add, respect 309.79' — is a sizing instruction, not a directional one, and the account sits at 12.06% against 87.9% cash earning zero. With 12% already at the low end of that prescribed band, the direction of the marginal dollar should be up, not flat; the neutral chair was right that a 0.12 ceiling treats a non-yielding cash balance as free when it is not, and the aggressive chair was right that an unexplained gap-down on a record-margin 10-Q is concentrated, not organic, distribution.

But the bear wins the execution and risk debate, and that governs the size rather than the direction. The tape evidence is specific and mutually confirming: price is below the 10-EMA (316.81), below a falling VWMA (329.58 on 07-30 → 320.14 on 08-07 — the average dollar transacted is at a loss), and below the Bollinger midline (323.43); the bounce volume fell every session to 0.41x the 132.5M distribution day; MACD is 0.878 against a 4.059 signal with a −3.181 histogram and is near its first zero-line cross since 06-30; RSI 47.58 is dead neutral against a technical filter that requires >55 to confirm and <45 to invalidate; and the 50-SMA slope has collapsed from +3.07 to +0.49 over six sessions. Both the aggressive and neutral chairs were also factually corrected on the same point and I accept the correction: the 07-31 high was 310.69 and the first post-gap close was 309.38, so all four bounce closes sit inside the unfilled 310.69–329.59 gap, having repaired only its bottom sliver — that is not 'four sessions deep.' The bear also landed three unrebutted analytical hits: a $13.3B gross-intangible increase offset almost exactly by $13.5B of other non-current liabilities (flagged twice for note-level verification); CFO growth of +43.1% flattered by a $10.8B cash-tax benefit plus working-capital releases, putting underlying cash growth nearer mid-teens-to-20%; and buybacks down 12% YoY ($62.1B vs $70.6B), which thins the EPS-accretion lever and means management slowed, not accelerated, its buying. The bull's inventory rebuttal (finished goods −4.1%, raw materials +260% = pre-ramp component stockpile) is the better reading and I accept it, but a $5.5B component commitment carries a non-zero write-down the bull priced at zero, and App Store revenue +0.6% with downloads −4% is a genuine Services-quality warning.

The account's own trade log seals the sizing argument: we went 20% → 12% in two sessions (63.6 shares bought 08-06 at $20.00 in fees, 25.2 sold 08-07 at $7.84), cumulative fees $27.83 and realized P&L −$88.47. That round trip inside a chop zone is bad process, and going to 0.15 — three points, not eight — with pre-defined add and cut conditions is precisely how the whipsaw is avoided. I reject the aggressive chair's 0.20: a repeat of the 07-31 gap from 313.33 opens near 286, through the 297 stop and the 300 floor, which is roughly 1.2% of total equity at 15% but closer to 1.7% at 20%, and the neutral chair was right that 20% is not justified by a bounce on 0.41x volume before 316.81 or 300 resolves. The 297 stop is a narrative condition, not an implemented order, so I size as if it can be gapped. I also reject the neutral chair's 0.135 as too fine a distinction to trade: 0.15 is already only a three-point add and lands at the low end of the prescribed band, so shading another 1.5 points buys negligible gap protection while weakening the expression of a decisively stronger fundamental case.

What would change it: add toward 0.20 on a daily close above 316.81 on ≥55–60M shares with acceptance above 320.14, or toward 0.20–0.22 on a 300–303 retest closing back above 305 on expanding volume provided RSI prints a higher low than 40.34 (the highest-quality entry, and where the bulk of remaining cash should be reserved). Cut to ≤0.08 on a close below 300.00 (07-31 gap low, lower Bollinger 300.84, ~1.5% under the 50-SMA); exit to 0 on a close below 297 or a confirmed MACD zero-line cross combined with a negative 50-SMA slope; reassess to Sell at FQ4 on gross margin below 48%, inventory above $13–14B with revenue growth decelerating below 10%, or note-level disclosure that the $13.3B intangible is impairment-prone. Explicitly not used because not supplied: the identity of the 07-31 catalyst (213 eligible news records, only 20 supplied, all timestamped 2026-08-06 — 07-31 through 08-05 is a void), note-level detail on the intangible or deferred obligations, an Apple-specific tariff-refund figure (the $166B headline spans Apple, Amazon and Nike with no company split), corroboration of the September iPhone 18/foldable/CEO-transition items beyond a single uncorroborated contributor post, and any live market quote behind the fundamental report's buyback-implied $300–$380 anchor.
